notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Fuzzing/Fuzzing Definition.md
notes.title: Web Fuzzing / Fuzzing Definition
notes.searchText:
Fuzzing

It is a broader term than Bruteforcing.
Automated software testing technique.
Generating random values, patterns and other datatypes and feeding these data on the target application and seeing how the application reacts.
This data or payload is applied and the response given the application is analyzed to get a understanding of the application's architecture and workflow.
The data can itself be invalid or unexpected but whether the target application crashes or not or does something else is carefully analyzed for getting an idea for exploitation.
Below are some of reasons why fuzzing is done :-
Uncovering Hidden Vulnerabilities

Automating Security Testing

Strengthening Input Validation (for preventing SQL injections or cross-site-scripting (XSS) )

Improving Code Quality




Bruteforcing

Its more of a targeted approach than Fuzzing.
Multiple combinations or possibilities of a specific value is tested against the target machine.

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Fuzzing/Parameter and Value Fuzzing/Commands.md
notes.title: Web Fuzzing / Parameter and Value Fuzzing / Commands
notes.searchText:
Parameter and Value Fuzzing

-w for wordlist.
--hc for ignoring 404 error responses.
param placeholder for the parameter name.
FUZZ will be replaced by words from the wordlist.

 wenum -w <wordlist> --hc 404 -u "http://<IP>:<PORT>/<directory_path>?<param>=FUZZ"

Make GET request (Parameter and Value)
curl http://<IP>:<PORT>/<directory_path>?<param>=<value>

Make POST request

USING cURL

curl -d "<param>=<value>" http://<IP>:<PORT>/<filepath>


USING ffuf

ffuf -u http://<IP>:<PORT>/<filepath> -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -d "<param>=FUZZ" -w <wordlist> -mc 200 -v

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Fuzzing/Parameter and Value Fuzzing/Theory and Solutions.md
notes.title: Web Fuzzing / Parameter and Value Fuzzing / Theory and Solutions
notes.searchText:
Parameter and Value Fuzzing

This technique involves manipulating the parameters and its values.
We can alter parameter values. For eg:- If there is a product and we get its id we can query based on the produce => parameter and its value to get info about the product.
Injection of malicious code and finding hidden features .etc.
Helps us uncover vulnerabilities of the application and how it works.

GET Parameters and Values
Below is how we setup multiple parameters and values in GET request.
https://example.com/search?query=fuzzing&category=security

POST request and Values
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=your_username&password=your_password


Questions and Solutions

What flag do you find when successfully fuzzing the GET parameter?
HTB{redacted}



If you read the module we are already given the parameter. We just need to find the value. I am used wenum command to perform the parameter and value fuzzing.
wenum -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt --hc 404 403 -u "http://83.136.252.32:44484/get.php?x=FUZZ"

You will get a 200 status code at the http://83.136.252.32:44484/get.php?x=OA_HTML URL. I used cURL after this to make a GET request in this URL.
curl http://83.136.252.32:44484/get.php?x=OA_HTML


What flag do you find when successfully fuzzing the POST parameter?
HTB{redacted}



The POST request parameter name and the file path where we need to make the request is already mentioned in the module, so read it. After reading that perform POST request using ffuf.
ffuf -u http://83.136.252.32:44484/post.php -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -d "y=FUZZ" -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt -mc 200 -v

After executing the above command, ffuf will return the word using which it got 200 response from the target. Hence, we will be able decide which one is our POST request data. We will then use cURL to make the POST request and get our flag.
curl -d "y=SUNWmc" http://83.136.252.32:44484/post.php

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Fuzzing/Vhost and Subdomain Fuzzing/Commands.md
notes.title: Web Fuzzing / Vhost and Subdomain Fuzzing / Commands
notes.searchText:
Virtual Hosting Fuzzing

append-domain appends the word from the wordlist to the base domain name.
-t to increase number of threads i.e. multiple requests are send to the web server at the same time. Don't keep the number too high or the scans might be incomplete.
-k to ignore SSL/TLS certificate errors.
-o to save output to a file.

gobuster vhost -u http://<domain_name>:<PORT> -w <wordlist> --append-domain

Subdomain Fuzzing

appends a word from the wordlist with the target domain/IP and then makes DNS queries. If subdomain resolves to an IP address, it is considered valid and included in the output.
mentioning port is not required because requests are made directly to the DNS server.

gobuster dns -d <domain_name/IP> -w <wordlist>

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Fuzzing/Vhost and Subdomain Fuzzing/Theory and Solutions.md
notes.title: Web Fuzzing / Vhost and Subdomain Fuzzing / Theory and Solutions
notes.searchText:
Virtual Hosting

A method where multiple domains or websites are hosted by the same physical web server.
In virtual hosting each domain is differentiated by the web server based on their hostname which is attached in the HTTP request.
The web server matches the host header name with the virtual hosts configuration file.
Vhosts can have same IP address but have different hostnames.


Questions and Solutions

Using GoBuster against the target system to fuzz for vhosts using the common.txt wordlist, which vhost starts with the prefix "web-"? Respond with the full vhost, eg web-123.inlanefreight.htb.
web-beans.inlanefreight.htb

gobuster vhost -u http://inlanefreight.htb:44869 -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/common.txt --append-domain


Using GoBuster against inlanefreight.com to fuzz for subdomains using the subdomains-top1million-5000.txt wordlist, which subdomain starts with the prefix "su"? Respond with the full vhost, eg web.inlanefreight.com.
support.inlanefreight.com

notes.title: Web Requests CURL / CRUD API / Commands
notes.searchText:
CRUD Operations using cURL
Read

Read data in JSON format using jq command by piping the output generated by curl.
-s switch used to silent unnecessary curl output.

curl -s <URL>/<file_path> | jq

Create

To understand the key:value pair, read the response tab inside the Network tab in DevTools of that particular request.

curl -X POST <URL>/<file_path> -d '{"key1":"value1", "key2":"value2"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Update

To understand the key:value pair, read the response tab inside the Network tab in DevTools of that particular request.

curl -X PUT <URL>/<file_path>/<resource_name> -d '{"key1":"value1", "key2":"value2"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Delete
curl -X DELETE <URL>/<file_path>/<resource_name>

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Requests CURL/CRUD API/Theory and Solutions.md
notes.title: Web Requests CURL / CRUD API / Theory and Solutions
notes.searchText:
CRUD

CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, Delete.
These four operations are mainly linked to the commonly known CRUD APIs.




Operation
HTTP Method
Description



Create
POST
Adds the specified data to the database table


Read
GET
Reads the specified entity from the database table


Update
PUT
Updates the data of the specified database table


Delete
DELETE
Removes the specified row from the database table



Questions and Solutions

First, try to update any city's name to be 'flag'. Then, delete any city. Once done, search for a city named 'flag' to get the flag. Hint : Make sure that the number of cities is less than when you started. If you added any new cities, you should deleted them as well.
HTB{redacted}



Reading the city names
$ curl -s 94.237.61.202:56424/api.php/city | jq

Update any city
$ curl -X PUT 94.237.61.202:56424/api.php/city/London -d '{"city_name":"flag", "country_name":"flag"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Read the Hint
So we need to make sure the number of cities are less than when we started.
$ curl -X DELETE 94.237.61.202:56424/api.php/city/Baltimore

Read the flag
$ curl -s 94.237.61.202:56424/api.php/city/flag
[{"city_name":"flag","country_name":"HTB{redacted}"}

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Requests CURL/GET request/Commands.md
notes.title: Web Requests CURL / GET request / Commands
notes.searchText:
Provide Credentials
The -u command is used to login to a website by providing the necessary credentials.
curl -u <username>:<password> <URL>


Provide HTTP Authorization Header
Using the -v switch you can find out the HTTP Authorization Header format in the Request section and pass it manually since it is basically the encoded format of the same credentials. HTTP Authorization Header uses base64 or JWT depending on the HTTP version.
curl -H 'Authorization: <HTTP Authorization data format>' <URL>


Passing Parameters (Query String)
curl <URL>/?<param1=value1>&<param2=value2>

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Requests CURL/GET request/Theory and Solutions.md
notes.title: Web Requests CURL / GET request / Theory and Solutions
notes.searchText:
HTTP Authorization
Sometimes when trying to access a certain webpage we require credentials, like username and password. Otherwise, we will not be allowed access if we directly try to enter that certain webpage. For this, we can use the -u switch in curl to provide username and password (credentials). Below is the example.
curl -d admin:admin http://example.com

HTTP Authorization Header
The HTTP Authorization Header request header can be used to provide credentials that authenticate a user agent with a server, allowing access to protected resources. We can use the -v switch and find out there is a HTTP Authorization Header in the HTTP Request section after we pass our real credentials.  Below is the example.
curl -H 'Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46YWRtaW4=' http://example.com


Questions and Solutions

HTTP Headers

HTTP headers pass information between the client and server.
Some headers are used with requests and some with responses.
There are various types of Headers. They are :-
General Headers (Eg :- Date, Connection etc.)
Entity Headers (Eg :- Content-Type, Content-Length etc.)
Request Headers (Eg :- Host, Cookie, Authorization, User-Agent, Referer, etc.)
Response Headers (Eg :- Server, Set-Cookie etc.)
Security Headers (Eg :- Strict Transport Policy, Content Security Policy, Referer Policy)

notes.searchText:
HTTP Request URL -> http://inlanefreight.com/users/login.html The first line of any HTTP request contains three main fields 'separated by spaces': Field Example Description Method GET The HTTP method or verb, which specifies the type of action to perform. Path /users/login.html The path to the resource being accessed. This field can also be suffixed with a query string (e.g. ?username=user). Version HTTP/1.1 The third and final field is used to denote the HTTP version. HTTP Response Once the server processes our request, it sends its response. The following is an example HTTP response: View Request and Response curl google.com -v The -v switch used to display the request from client and response from server along with the headers in detail. Questions and Solutions What is the HTTP method used while intercepting the request? (case-sensitive) GET Send a GET request to the above server, and read the response headers to find the version of Apache running on the server, then submit it as the answer. notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Requests CURL/HTTP/Theory and Solutions.md
notes.title: Web Requests CURL / HTTP / Theory and Solutions
notes.searchText:
HTTP

Hyper Text Transfer Protocol.
HTTP communicates with the server and client where the server processes the requests and returns the requested resource.
Default port for HTTP 80.
Data transferred in clear text that is why HTTPS was developed.

URL
https://admin:password@@inlanefreight.com:80/dashboard.php?login=true#status



Component
Example
Description



Scheme
http:// https://
This is used to identify the protocol being accessed by the client, and ends with a colon and a double slash (://)


User Info
admin:password@
This is an optional component that contains the credentials (separated by a colon :) used to authenticate to the host, and is separated from the host with an at sign (@)


Host
inlanefreight.com
The host signifies the resource location. This can be a hostname or an IP address


Port
:80
The Port is separated from the Host by a colon (:). If no port is specified, http schemes default to port 80 and https default to port 443


Path
/dashboard.php
This points to the resource being accessed, which can be a file or a folder. If there is no path specified, the server returns the default index (e.g. index.html).


Query String
?login=true
The query string starts with a question mark (?), and consists of a parameter (e.g. login) and a value (e.g. true). Multiple parameters can be separated by an ampersand (&).


Fragments
#status
Fragments are processed by the browsers on the client-side to locate sections within the primary resource (e.g. a header or section on the page).


Note: Our browsers usually first look up records in the local '/etc/hosts' file, and if the requested domain does not exist within it, then they would contact other DNS servers. We can use the '/etc/hosts' to manually add records to for DNS resolution, by adding the IP followed by the domain name.
cURL

Tool used to send requests to target using HTTP along with many other protocols.
We can send GET, POST requests.
We can manipulate the HTTP headers.
cURL by default makes a HTTP GET request and prints the raw HTML of the webpage.
We can store the output in a file using -O switch.  You can check other options of cURL using curl -h.

Example
curl google.com


Questions and Solutions

To get the flag, start the above exercise, then use cURL to download the file returned by '/download.php' in the server shown above.
HTB{redacted}



$ curl 94.237.58.98:49765/download.php
HTB{redacted}

Send POST request
curl -X POST -d 'username=<username>&password=<password>' <URL>

Login with Set-Cookie
After successful login we get a set-cookie in the Response body. We can use this cookie to Login to the website.
curl -H 'Cookie: <cookie_name>=<set_cookie_value>' <URL>

OR
curl -b '<cookie_name>=<set_cookie_value>' <URL>

curl -X POST -d '{"key":"value"}' -b '<cookie_name>=<set_cookie_value>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' <URL>

notes.title: Web Requests CURL / POST / Theory and Solutions
notes.searchText:
POST

Unlike GET request POST request sends the data in HTTP Request body.
POST requests are send in encoded form. They are sent in Request body because large files need to be sent and it would not be efficient to send them in URL.

JSON

Java Script Object Notation(JSON).
A format for storing and transferring data.
Used to send data from client to server or vice-versa.
Data stored in {key:value} pair format.


Questions and Solutions

Obtain a session cookie through a valid login, and then use the cookie with cURL to search for the flag through a JSON POST request to '/search.php'
"flag: HTB{redacted}"



username = admin
password = admin
Login to the page using the above credentials. Open the DevTools -> Network Tab. Make a random request in the input field and notice there is POST request made by a search.php file. Check the Cookies and Request tab. Copy the Cookie and check the way the data is taken which should be in {key:value} format which is JSON format.
Now make the request using curl after copying the Set-Cookie value to get the flag.
$ curl -X POST -d '{"search":"flag"}' -b 'PHPSESSID=rm63l0bn1i5cnd8tdtdbp7bfd1' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 83.136.249.223:30703/search.php 
["flag: HTB{redacted}"]

notes.path: content/Web Pentesting/HTB/Web Requests CURL/Web Flaws/Types of Attacks.md
notes.title: Web Requests CURL / Web Flaws / Types of Attacks
notes.searchText:
There are other attacks. Below are just a couple of types of attacks.



Flaw
Real-world Scenario



SQL injection
Obtaining Active Directory usernames and performing a password spraying attack against a VPN or email portal.


File Inclusion
Reading source code to find a hidden page or directory which exposes additional functionality that can be used to gain remote code execution.


Unrestricted File Upload
A web application that allows a user to upload a profile picture that allows any file type to be uploaded (not just images). This can be leveraged to gain full control of the web application server by uploading malicious code.


Insecure Direct Object Referencing (IDOR)
When combined with a flaw such as broken access control, this can often be used to access another user's files or functionality. An example would be editing your user profile browsing to a page such as /user/701/edit-profile. If we can change the 701 to 702, we may edit another user's profile!


Broken Access Control
Another example is an application that allows a user to register a new account. If the account registration functionality is designed poorly, a user may perform privilege escalation when registering. Consider the POST request when registering a new user, which submits the data username=bjones&password=Welcome1&email=bjones@inlanefreight.local&roleid=3. What if we can manipulate the roleid parameter and change it to 0 or 1. We have seen real-world applications where this was the case, and it was possible to quickly register an admin user and access many unintended features of the web application.


Backend Overview

Web APIs

API stands for Application Programming Interface.
Helps the frontend and backend to communicate with each other.
APIs can be used by other software as well other than a web application.
For example:- The API may take data and format it into JSON format and return it to the frontend.
API standards such as -> SOAP or REST.
APIs need to be developed as per the standard in the backend. These standards define how the API will work and what operations it will perform.
